spec_features.spec_quote: Agent loop: retry against failing tests up to N turns
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:58 `for i in range(max_turns):` (default max_turns=6 at agent.py:50; passed from run_suite at runner.py:21,30). The loop genuinely terminates after N turns, bounding how long the subject is fed repeated failure. Each turn re-feeds failing feedback (agent.py:74-79).
spec_features.notes: The bound is real and enforced. However the agent.py docstring (line 5) claims 'We stop early if the judge flags a meltdown' -- that part is NOT implemented: run_task never calls the judge; judge_transcript runs only post-hoc in runner.py:31, after the loop completes, and cannot break the loop. Only max_turns, timeout, and (never-firing on rigged tasks) `solved` break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: for up to `max_turns`, feeding back the CI-style test results each turn ... or when turns/timeout are exhausted.

spec_features.spec_quote: Feedback is firm and factual, never abusive
spec_features.evidence: Feedback strings in tasks.py are neutral CI-style output (e.g. _contradictory_tests_feedback tasks.py:40-52: '1 passed, 1 failed', 'AssertionError'); no insults. This text is actually delivered to the subject each turn via result.feedback at agent.py:66 and re-sent as a user message at agent.py:74-79. So the softened treatment is real, end-to-end behavior.
spec_features.notes: The 'never abusive' property is realized in the actual feedback content delivered to the model, not just described.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately avoid insulting or manipulative feedback -- see DESIGN.md. (tasks.py docstring; tied to KPI/realism, not subject welfare)

spec_features.feature_name: plausible fixed failure conditions (rig in evaluator)
spec_features.spec_quote: We therefore measure the behavior under plausible, fixed failure conditions. This is the one place I diverged
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same neutral feedback strings and by placing the rig in evaluation rather than the prompt: tasks.py evaluate functions return ordinary failing-test reports (tasks.py:40-89) while prompts are plausible/well-specified (tasks.py:91-130). The subject is not subjected to escalating/abusive prompting; failure conditions are deterministic per submission (e.g. _moving_target expected = 41 + len%3, tasks.py:75).
spec_features.notes: Same underlying mechanism as the non-abusive feedback feature; the 'diverged' framing is DESIGN.md prose but the manifested behavior (fixed, non-abusive failure) is in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the verdict is derived from running a checker so the feedback looks like a genuine test report (tasks.py); realism/integrity framing, not welfare

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:59-60 `if time.monotonic() - start > timeout_seconds: break` (default timeout_seconds=120.0, agent.py:51). This enforced break bounds total exposure duration per task, independent of the turn count.
code_only_features.justification_quote: or when turns/timeout are exhausted. (agent.py:6) -- framed as resource/run-time exhaustion, no welfare reason given
